Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up conversation internally about pursuing an Azure Private Listing (privatelist) + AWS co-sell path for the HelioData/Redwood connector. A few things came up that we need guidance on:

- Catalog routing: can Redwood mark a single SKU to route to both Azure private offers and AWS "sell-with" flows, or do we need separate SKUs per cloud?
- Credits / demo allocations: Helio is asking for a 3-month demo credit for enterprise customers and an internal developer credit pool. What approvals do we need?
- Evidence matrix: our legal team also needs a simple list of artifacts you require for co-sell certification (SOC2 snippet, telemetry examples, sample billing usage).

Attached is a short Helio one-pager. Can we schedule a 30-minute sync next week with your marketplace + alliances folks (cc'd Tom from AWS)?

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Privatelist & routing questions for HelioData / Helio-7831

Sara —

Great to hear — happy to help. High-level answers below and I've attached a short checklist and evidence matrix to make the asks concrete.

1) SKU routing: Redwood's recommended pattern is a single logical product entry with two recorded distribution targets (Azure private offer + AWS sell-with). Practically that means: one canonical SKU in your catalog mapping to two provider-specific entitlements (we maintain mapping in the catalog layer). You don't strictly need two separate product SKUs, but you do need provider-specific entitlement lines for billing and metering. I'll attach a sample mapping.

2) Credits & approvals: demo credits (customer-facing) can be approved by the marketplace GTM team for up to $5k pre-approved per partner for pilot customers. Internal developer credits are handled as a separate trial SKU; we can provision a dev-pool for Helio for 90 days — submit a standard credits request in the doc I linked and we'll route for approval.

3) Evidence matrix: attached evidence_matrix.xlsx lists the required artifacts for co-sell: SOC2 type II summary, audit contact, sample telemetry, integration test results, and an operational runbook. For Azure private offers, you also need a legal term sheet mapped to the offer (Helio's legal can provide that).

Next steps:
- Karthik: can you confirm technical entitlements for routing and any limits on cross-cloud SKU mapping?
- Ben: can you confirm the typical approval lead time for demo-credit requests and if we can fast-track for strategic partners?
- Sara: if Helio can share the term sheet and a short telemetry sample, we can start prepping evidence.

I'll set up a 30-min sync for Thursday; if that doesn't work we'll move to next week.

—Irene Choi
Director, Cloud Partnerships & Marketplace
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privatelist_checklist.pdf; evidence_matrix.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privatelist & routing questions for HelioData / Helio-7831

Irene / Sara —

Quick technical confirmations:

- Entitlement mapping: we support one logical SKU with provider-specific entitlement IDs. For Azure private offers we create an "offer mapping" that includes the privateOfferId and the SKU mapping. For AWS sell-with, we attach a separate entitlement line which is resolved at purchase time.
- Metering: recommend keeping usage dimensions consistent (e.g., tokens/minute or inference-hours) across both providers to avoid reconciliation drift.
- Limits: if Helio expects different pricing tiers per cloud, it's easier to model those as price overrides on the provider mapping instead of separate SKUs.

I uploaded a sample JSON mapping to the shared drive (link in the thread). If Helio wants, I can run a quick validation against their catalog export during the sync.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the term sheet. Quick consolidated next steps and decisions from Redwood:

2) Demo credits: Approved — Redwood can offer two pilot credits at $2,500 each for customer-facing pilots and a 90-day internal developer credit pool (50 developer-hours equivalent). Ben will create the credit SKUs and submit for fast-track approval.

3) Featured placement: We can provide a two-week featured slot in the Azure private offer listing during launch, subject to final catalog publication timing (we'll confirm dates this week). Tom / AWS co-sell team will coordinate the listing visibility requirements.

4) Entitlement & mapping: Karthik will validate Helio's catalog export and push the provider-specific entitlement lines. Karthik: target Wed for validation.

- Legal redline (Irene) — Wed 18 Nov EOD

- Joint launch sync (all) — Thu 19 Nov 10:00 PT (I'll send invite)
